light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but growth slows and the leaves stay small

items: Trained up a tree trunk or totem

snap: A climbing philodendron with glossy, dark green leaves held on bright orange stems. The orange against the green makes it a favourite with collectors. It grows bigger leaves as it climbs, and likes warmth and humid air. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Native to the rainforests of northern South America, around French Guiana and nearby parts of Brazil, where it climbs tree trunks with aerial roots. Young plants carry small, heart-shaped leaves. As the vine climbs, the leaves grow longer, larger and wavier. With a pole to climb it can reach 1–2 m indoors.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Give it bright indirect light, warmth and humid air. Water when the top 3–5 cm of the mix is dry, use a chunky, airy aroid mix, and never leave the pot standing in water. Direct sun scorches the leaves and fades the orange stems. Keep it above 15°C and away from cold drafts. Dry air browns the leaf edges.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The stems, or petioles, are a bright orange-yellow that stands out against the deep green, glossy leaves. A moss pole makes the leaves larger and more elongated and wavy at the edges. Each new leaf opens from a pale bud sheath that later drops off. Wipe the leaves gently with a damp cloth to keep the gloss.
